title: Encoded PowerShell launched from Word macro
description: EDR flagged powershell.exe -enc spawned by WINWORD.EXE on WS-014, followed by an outbound connection to an unknown domain.
steps: Dump process tree and decode the base64 command
Pull the email that delivered invoice_q3.docm
Search other mailboxes for the same attachment
root_cause: Phishing email with a macro-enabled Word attachment
remediation: Isolated host, reset user credentials, blocked sender domain and C2 domain, purged the email org-wide
feedback: Helpful: checking the email source first saved time
lessons: For encoded PowerShell, check the parent process and the delivering email before anything else

title: Phishing link harvesting Microsoft 365 credentials
description: User reported an email with a link to a fake login page. Proxy logs show the user submitted credentials.
steps: Confirm in proxy logs who clicked
Review sign-in logs for the account
remediation: Reset password, revoked sessions, blocked domain, notified affected users
feedback: Partially helpful: missed checking for new inbox rules
lessons: After a phishing click, always check mailbox rules and MFA registrations

title: SSH brute force against bastion host
description: Over 2000 failed SSH logins from one external IP in 15 minutes, no successful login.
steps: Check auth.log for any success from the source IP
Block the IP at the firewall
root_cause: Automated internet scanning; password auth still enabled
remediation: Blocked IP, disabled password authentication, enabled fail2ban
lessons: Disable password SSH on exposed hosts; rate-limit logins

title: Scheduled task persistence after PowerShell download
description: New scheduled task running a PowerShell script from a temp directory, created minutes after an encoded PowerShell execution.
steps: List scheduled tasks created in the last 24 hours
Check for the same C2 IP across hosts
Remove the task after collecting evidence
root_cause: Attacker persistence after an earlier encoded PowerShell compromise
remediation: Removed scheduled task, isolated server, rebuilt from clean image, rotated service account passwords
feedback: Helpful: linking to the C2 IP from an earlier incident was the key
lessons: Encoded PowerShell is often followed by persistence. Search for scheduled tasks and the same C2 IP
